answer: Sunk-cost forge: identities must pay a small, non-refundable compute deposit whose difficulty is seeded by the account's creation block hash, so an attacker must mine each clone's registration separately rather than batch-mint them. The chain keeps a river of these deposits flowing to validators, and a re-registration after any lapse requires re-paying at a rate that rises with prior account age. Each alias thus costs real, unrecoverable work proportional to the fleet size, and every extra pigment of identity adds a fresh per-clone mining bill that scales linearly with count.
